record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: flat energy dependence of pion BEC source radius in e+e− annihilation
record.original_question: In electron-positron annihilation into hadrons, why is the pion-pair Bose-Einstein-correlation emitter dimension rππ, where r is the Gaussian source-size parameter in the two-boson correlation C₂(Q) = 1 + λ₂ exp(-r²Q²) with Q² = -(p₁ - p₂)², essentially independent of the center-of-mass energy √s_ee even though the average hadron multiplicity increases with energy; and what source model can quantitatively account for that flat rππ distribution?

evidence.quote: Assuming the emitter to be a sphere of a Gaussian distribution, the correlation of pairs of identical bosons can be parametrised by C2(Q) = 1 + λ2e−r2Q2 where Q2 = −(p1 − p2)2 and p1 and p2 are the four momenta of the two bosons.

As for the rππ values obtained from the e+e− annihilation analyses, they are seen in Fig. 1 to be essentially independent of √see as it is generally accepted that the small deviations from a constant value are due to the non-uniformity of the chosen experimental procedures. Since e.g. the average hadron multiplicity increases with energy this flat r distribution poses a theoretical challenge.
As seen, the r behaviour extracted from this simplified model, which rises by only ∼3.5% from 10 to 90 GeV CM energy, already describes nicely experimental situation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider electron–positron annihilation into hadrons at center-of-mass energy √s. Two-particle Bose–Einstein correlations of identically charged pions are parametrized, assuming a Gaussian spherical emitter, by
  C₂(Q) = 1 + λ₂ exp(−r²Q²),
where Q² = −(p₁ − p₂)² is built from the four-momenta p₁, p₂ of the two pions, λ₂ is an incoherence parameter, and r = r_{ππ} is the Gaussian source-size parameter.

Empirically, across √s ranging from roughly 10 GeV to 91 GeV, the extracted r_{ππ} is essentially independent of √s, even though the mean charged-hadron multiplicity ⟨n⟩ grows substantially with √s.

(a) Provide a theoretical explanation, within the framework of multiparticle production in e⁺e⁻ annihilation, of why r_{ππ} should be (nearly) independent of √s despite the growth of ⟨n⟩.
(b) Construct an explicit source model — for example, treating hadronic jets as independent pion-emitting sources and relating r_{ππ} to the normalized factorial cumulant moments of the multiplicity distribution — that quantitatively reproduces the observed flat behavior of r_{ππ}(√s) over 10 GeV ≲ √s ≲ 91 GeV.
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up work proposes that treating hadron jets as independent pion sources, combined with the dependence of normalized factorial cumulant moments on the number of sources, quantitatively reproduces the nearly energy-independent r_{ππ} measured in e⁺e⁻ annihilation between 10 and 91 GeV (rising only ~3.5%). This provides a quantitative model that fits the data, so the phenomenological challenge is partially resolved, though a fully first-principles derivation is not established.

status_evidence.title: The particle emitter size dependence on energy in e+e− annihilations into hadrons
status_evidence.snippet: The nearly energy independent hadron emitter dimension measured in e+e− annihilation in the energy range 10 to 91 GeV via the Bose–Einstein correlation of two identical charged pions is shown to be well accounted for by choosing the hadron jets as independent pion sources.
status_evidence.claim: A jets-as-independent-sources model quantitatively accounts for the flat r_{ππ}(√s).

status_evidence.title: Bose–Einstein correlations - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Bose–Einstein correlations are the only method for the determination of sizes and lifetimes of sources of elementary particles.
status_evidence.claim: BEC are the standard tool for extracting emitter source size.
